newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE volume sets record high in 1996.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE volume sets record high in 1996.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Friday 1996 was its busiest year ever, with 167.9 million contracts traded.
Volume was up 27 percent on 1996 and nearly 10 percent up on LIFFE's previous busiest year in 1994, LIFFE said.
Annual average daily volume rose to 661,183 contracts with nominal average daily value of 159.5 billion stg.
In December, 11.3 million contracts were traded, 45 percent more than December 1995, making it the busiest December ever.
During the month, the three month Euroswiss option and the FTSE 100 European option set daily volume records of 3,125 on December 10 and 52,568 on December 20 respectively, LIFFE said.
Daniel Hodson, LIFFE's chief executive, said the exchange has consolidated its number one position in Europe with trading volumes greater than the next two exchanges combined.

"This the best possible basis for achieving our ambition to be the world centre for euro derivatives trading, when EMU takes place," he said in a news release. "This will be our overriding aim in 1997."
LIFFE said October was its busiest month in 1996 with average daily volume of 800,021 futures and options traded representing a nominal average daily value of 190.10 billion stg.
Open interest reached a record high of 6.7 million contracts on November 15. It ended the year at 5.1 million compared with 3.8 million in 1995 and 3.1 million in 1994.
The fastest growing contract was the three-month Eurolira option, which jumped 852 percent to 953.558 contracts.

Other big gainers included three-month Euroswiss futures, up 89 percent in the year, FTSE 100 index options, up 52 percent, BTP futures up 31 percent, BTP options up 117 percent and three month Euromark futures up 41 percent.
